findings.issue: ExprDepthBounded is exprDepth e ≤ 55. TemplateDepthBounded checks only t.guard and omits deltas.amount and supplyDeltas.amount. encodeExpr adds constructor objects; typed-execute guard sits at JSON depth 7 and delta amount at 9. Source AST 55 is not a proof of JSON depth ≤ 64. Scanner increments then depth>64; parser refuses stack.length≥64 before push. Both admit 64 containers and refuse the 65th. ProbeR9: wrapNow 55 (AST 56) guard encodes nest 62, decodeBytes ok-eq, Nat.ble 55 is false (excluded by the cap). wrapNow 57 (AST 58) nest 64, decodeBytes ok-eq. wrapNow 58 (AST 59) nest 65, resourceLimit maxDepth. wrapNow 63 as delta amount, guard .now: guard depth 1, amount 64, nest 72, scan/parse/decode all maxDepth. TemplateDepthBounded would hold on the guard. No kernel SupportedIR proof was synthesised (Decidable ExprDepthBounded failed). Predicate text plus runtime are separate.

config.catalog.length ≤ 4096 does not bound component privateCells/exports/imports/operations or operation inputs/outputs. EnvelopeLengthBounds omits claimed_next_state.capabilities.entries. Scanner comma-count throws when cnt+1>4096, so 4097 elements pass the scanner. decodeBytes remaps every parseCanonicalJson error, including resourceLimit max_array_length, to notJsonObject. ProbeR9: catalog length 1, privateCells 4097, encode 200173 bytes, scan ok, parse max_array_length, decode notJsonObject. Same for 4097 operation inputs (130564 bytes) and 4097 claimed_next_state capabilities (369468 bytes). No kernel SupportedIR proof. Exact byte-length SerializedByteBound is not this defect.
